thread:
support_lead: Heads-up — after last night's rate-policy rollout we started getting a steady stream of 429s from AcmeCorp around 02:10 UTC. Canaries looked fine but their traffic is very bursty. Posting what we have so we can decide rollback vs tweak.

devin: Confirming. Pager showed a sharp jump in 429 counts and client complaints. I pulled a couple of sample request IDs.

maria: Any header evidence the gateway applied the new limits? Ask customer to paste X-RateLimit-* headers if possible.

support_lead: Yes — from our logs a few responses include headers like:```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 02:12:34 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700
Content-Type: application/json
```

james: That Reset value looks large — maybe policy uses a long window. Also I see their traffic has short peaks of many concurrent requests for streaming sessions. Batching + small window would blow through tokens quickly.

ana: (typo) ana: I'm on infra logs — the shard serving their region had backlog increase ~02:08 then request latency rose ~30ms before 429s. No sign of OOM.

devin: Repro steps from support: they were doing ~40 parallel connections, each starting small chat interactions every 1–2s for a burst of 90s. They hit limits predictably.

support_lead: Customer says they saw 429s even though overall RPS is below pre-rollout numbers; it's the per-client burst cap that mattered. They want ETA to fix.

james: Options: 1) rollback policy for all customers (fast, broad), 2) rollback only for AcmeCorp (targeted), 3) tweak policy to allow short bursts (increase burst window or add leaky-bucket smoothing), 4) advise customer to client-side backoff.

maria: I'd prefer targeted rollback for now. We can push a policy variant keyed to their org id and leave others on new limits. Rollback steps below.

deploy-bot: canary push: rate-policy-v3 -> canary @ 2025-11-05T01:30:00Z. status: SUCCESS.

sre-bot: alert: 429 rate exceeded threshold (5min) on shard us-east-1-a. count=842 -> trigger paging to eng-oncall.

devin: If we target rollback we need to: 1) create policy override for org:acmecorp, 2) set burst window back to previous value, 3) push config, 4) verify headers served, 5) monitor 429 rate for 15–30m.

maria: I'll create the override. Quick note: make sure the override doesn't fall back to an unsafe default for other customers. Use explicit org rule.

ana: Also clear KV cache for policy decisions in edge proxies — there's a 30s TTL, so order matters: push the override, invalidate caches, then route traffic.

support_lead: Customer-facing message drafted: "We're rolling back a policy for your org to prevent rejections while we tune burst handling. We'll follow up with recommended client backoff parameters." Want to send asap once we see rollback live.

james: I'll stand by to run the rollback. Who triggers the config push? Is it infra or platform?

maria: Platform will push. I'm making the override now (branch: hotfix/acme-burst-rollback). Patch includes:```yaml
policy_overrides:
  - org: "acmecorp"
    rate_limit: 240
    burst_window_seconds: 120
```

devin: After push we'll check real-time logs: filter by org_id=acmecorp and response.code=429. Also verify X-RateLimit headers show the increased values.

deploy-bot: deploy job started: policy-service config push (hotfix/acme-burst-rollback) @ 2025-11-05T02:30:12Z

sre-bot: infra note: invalidating edge policy cache keys for org:acmecorp across us-east-*.

maria: Push complete. Patch applied to control-plane; edge caches invalidation initiated.

james: I see updated headers in the proxy logs for several requests:```X-RateLimit-Limit: 240
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 238
X-RateLimit-Reset: 119```

support_lead: Customer confirms they can proceed, 429s dropping. They saw a single 429 spike during the cache TTL window. :thumbsup:

ana: Monitoring: 429 rate fell from 842 -> 12 in 10m, latency normalized. Tracking will continue for 30m.

devin: Follow-ups: - postmortem to cover why canary missed this pattern, - add synthetic test for bursty parallel connections, - adjust rollout checklist to include sampling high-burst orgs.

maria: I'll file the postmortem and include suggested fixes: more conservative burst windows on first rollouts, targeted traffic sampling, and a canary traffic generator that mirrors 50–100 parallel clients.

support_lead: Customer satisfaction: asked for confirmation when we push a tuned policy. We'll coordinate a staged re-rollout after we validate the synthetic tests. Thanks all for quick response.

james: Adding runbook notes: if this repeats, prefer targeted override + cache invalidation rather than global rollback. Document the commands used:```# create override
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/policies/overrides 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
  -d '{"org":"acmecorp","rate_limit":240,"burst_window_seconds":120}'
# invalidate cache
curl -X POST https://edge-admin/cache/invalidate -d '{"org":"acmecorp"}'
```

support_lead: Closing here after monitoring window complete; will reopen thread if anything changes.
